old_value: {"id":"FLUJO-AGROMAX-u9a","title":"prep-progress.json concurrent pool writes can lose updates (last-completing-write-wins)","description":"src/lib/proxy-stage.ts runs up to PROXY_CONCURRENCY (default up to 4) clips in parallel via runPool(); each worker calls setStatus() -\u003e writePrepProgressJson(jobId, progress), which is the SAME shared in-memory 'progress' object mutated synchronously by every worker. writePrepProgressJson() (src/lib/jobs.ts) does 'await fs.mkdir(...)' BEFORE JSON.stringify+fs.writeFile — i.e. there is an await point between a worker's synchronous mutation and the eventual write of that JSON snapshot. Because multiple workers call this concurrently, the fs.writeFile calls for progress/prep-progress.json race: Node/libuv gives no ordering guarantee that writes STARTED earlier also COMPLETE earlier. If an earlier-started write (holding an older, smaller snapshot of 'progress') completes AFTER a later-started write (holding a newer, larger snapshot), the file on disk regresses to the stale snapshot and loses the newer clip's status update until the next transition overwrites it again. Impact is limited to UI progress display (X/N proxies, per-clip status) — it does not affect the final proxy .mp4 outputs (tmp+rename there is genuinely atomic per-file) — but a clip could get stuck showing 'pending'/'running' in the UI after it actually finished or errored, until another clip's status change happens to overwrite the file again (or forever if it was the last transition). Suggested fix: serialize prep-progress writes (e.g. a simple write-queue / mutex keyed by jobId) or write with a monotonic version check before persisting.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"chavezmiguel0114@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-07-21T20:45:00Z","created_by":"Miguel Chavez","updated_at":"2026-07-21T20:45:00Z"}
